items.q: Which oral patch carries the highest likelihood of severe dysplasia or carcinoma on biopsy?
items.exp: Erythroplakia, though rarer, shows severe dysplasia, carcinoma in situ or invasive cancer in most biopsies, far exceeding leukoplakia risk. Any persistent red patch mandates urgent biopsy.
r: Incorrect. Homogeneous white carries lower average risk.
Correct. Red velvet patches are most dangerous.
Incorrect. Lichen planus has low transformation risk bilaterally lacy.
Incorrect. Frictional lesions resolve removing trauma.
items.kp: Red patch in mouth: biopsy urgently, cancer until excluded.

items.q: Slow painless parotid tail mass with chondromyxoid (cartilage like) stroma and ductal elements is what?
items.exp: Pleomorphic (mixed) adenoma combines epithelial ducts with myoepithelial modified stroma resembling cartilage, commonest parotid tumour, benign but recurring if capsule ruptures at surgery.
r: Incorrect. Warthin is cystic oncocytic lymphoid in older smokers.
Correct. Mixed cartilage like tumour means pleomorphic adenoma.
Incorrect. High grade mucoepidermoid is malignant painful pattern.
Incorrect. Oncocytoma is solid oncocytic benign rarity.
items.kp: Cartilage in a salivary tumour equals pleomorphic adenoma.

items.q: Parotid mass with new facial nerve weakness most strongly indicates what?
items.exp: Facial palsy is a malignant sign in parotid masses (adenoid cystic or mucoepidermoid invasion) because benign tumours displace but rarely paralyse the nerve. Urgent imaging and tissue diagnosis follow.
r: Incorrect. Benign adenomas almost never palsies the nerve.
Correct. Nerve palsy maligns the mass until disproven.
Incorrect. Infection swells painfully without focal nerve invasion pattern.
Incorrect. Stones cause mealtime pain, not facial paralysis.
items.kp: Parotid lump plus weak face equals malignancy pathway.

items.q: Cribriform swiss cheese cylinders with perineural invasion and late pulmonary metastases describe which salivary cancer?
items.exp: Adenoid cystic carcinoma grows slowly but relentlessly along nerves causing pain, with cribriform basaloid cylinders around glycosaminoglycan pools, late haematogenous lung spread and protracted recurrence over decades.
r: Incorrect. Low grade mucoepidermoid is cystic mucus rich curable often.
Correct. Perineural swiss cheese cancer is adenoid cystic.
Incorrect. Acinic cell is serous differentiated parotid tumour better prognosis.
Incorrect. Ex pleomorphic arises in old adenomas without this classic pattern.
items.kp: Painful nerve hugging salivary cancer equals adenoid cystic.

items.q: Bilateral lacy white striae (Wickham) on buccal mucosa with skin flexor purple papules indicate which condition?
items.exp: Lichen planus gives reticular Wickham striae bilaterally with cutaneous purple polygonal pruritic papules, band like lymphocytic mucositis histologically and low malignant potential needing symptomatic care.
r: Incorrect. Leukoplakia is usually solitary non lacy premalignant patch.
Correct. Lacy bilateral striae mean lichen planus.
Incorrect. Candida wipes off leaving red base acutely.
Incorrect. Hairy leukoplakia corrugates lateral tongue in HIV (EBV).
items.kp: Lace on both cheeks equals lichen planus, not leukoplakia.

items.q: Commonest malignant salivary gland tumour composed of mucus, intermediate and epidermoid cells is what?
items.exp: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the commonest salivary malignancy (parotid and palate minor glands), graded by cystic proportion and cytology, with MAML2 translocation support in many cases.
r: Incorrect. Adenoid cystic is second classic with perineural habit.
Correct. Three cell mix means mucoepidermoid carcinoma.
Incorrect. Acinic cell is serous acinar differentiated.
Incorrect. Metastatic skin squamous lacks this glandular mix.
items.kp: Mucus plus squamoid in salivary gland equals mucoepidermoid.

items.q: Mealtime parotid pain and swelling in a dehydrated elderly patient most likely results from what?
o: Sialolithiasis duct stone with bacterial sialadenitis
items.exp: Salivary stones (submandibular most, parotid also) obstruct flow causing painful swelling at meals (saliva surge against block), secondarily infecting stagnant glands in dehydrated elderly patients.
r: Incorrect. Adenomas grow painlessly over years, not meals.
Correct. Meal timed pain means duct stone obstruction.
Incorrect. Sjogren dries chronically without meal colic.
Incorrect. Mumps swells bilaterally in younger viral illness.
items.kp: Pain when eating plus swollen gland equals stone in duct.

items.q: HPV driven oropharyngeal cancers characteristically arise where and stain how?
o: Tonsil and tongue base, p16 positive with better prognosis
items.exp: HPV (especially 16) E6 E7 inactivates p53 and Rb in tonsillar crypt epithelium causing p16 overexpressing oropharyngeal cancers in younger non smokers with nodal cystic spread yet better treatment response.
r: Incorrect. Floor cancers are tobacco field p16 negative usually.
Correct. Tonsil base plus p16 positivity means HPV driven.
Incorrect. Palate cancers follow tobacco and alcohol classically.
Incorrect. Lip cancers follow ultraviolet exposure.
items.kp: Young non smoker tonsil cancer: test p16 for HPV.

items.q: Warthin tumour classic patient and histology pairing is which?
o: Older male smoker, bilateral parotid tail cysts with oncocytic epithelium over lymphoid stroma
items.exp: Warthin (papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum) favours older male smokers, may be bilateral, with bilayered oncocytic cyst lining over dense lymphoid stroma, benign and possibly smoking related metaplasia.
r: Incorrect. That pairing describes pleomorphic adenoma demographics loosely.
Correct. Older smoker bilateral lymphoid cyst means Warthin.
Incorrect. Childhood cylinders do not occur in this benign tumour.
Incorrect. Lymphoma is the Sjogren complication, not Warthin definition.
items.kp: Smoker parotid cyst with lymphoid wall equals Warthin tumour.

items.q: Field cancerisation in oral cavity means what concept?
o: Chronic carcinogen exposure dysplasias wide mucosa causing multiple independent primaries over time
items.exp: Tobacco and alcohol bathe the whole aerodigestive mucosa, so genetically altered fields spawn second primary cancers independently after index tumours, mandating lifelong surveillance and cessation counselling.
r: Incorrect. Independent primaries, not metastases, define fields.
Correct. Wide exposed mucosa spawns multiple primaries.
Incorrect. Recall is chemotherapy radiation skin phenomenon.
Incorrect. No polyposis defines oral field change.
items.kp: Cured one oral cancer, watch the whole tract for the next.
